text:
alice.ops: heads up — multiple customers reporting p95/p99 spikes in eu1 starting ~2026-03-16T22:04Z. spike aligns with last night's kernel + cuda driver push to 525.4. noticed throughput drop on embedding endpoints and a few timeouts. creating thread to triage.

ben.sre: which endpoints & numbers? is this confined to a few hosts or across the fleet?

alice.ops: scope: embeddings (batching) + small-gen routes. p95 went from ~120ms -> ~600ms for small-gen, embeddings p95 200ms -> 1.1s, p99 up to 3s on some hosts. error rate (5xx/timeouts) ~0.18% overall but concentrated in eu1 region. affected hosts show high host-io wait.

carla-ml: no model changes rolled out from our side. traffic mix unchanged. could be runtime/kernel/driver.

incidents-bot: alert: eu1 cluster: host_io_wait > 40% on 12/48 nodes, nvme queue depth spikes detected, kernel dmesg showing blk_mq complaints.

ben.sre: can infra share dmesg/iostat outputs from affected hosts? also any recent firmware updates to nvme?

dmitri-eng: looking now. quick checks: iostat shows avg await spikes and util at 98% on nvme0 on host eu1-03. dmesg snapshot (truncated):

```
[ 12345.678901] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345678
[ 12345.679012] nvme 0000:04:00.0: queue depth exceeded
[ 12346.000000] stalling due to IO, task kworker/1:2 blocked for 120s
```

also seeing new driver module version "nvme-core 2.5.25" which matches the cuda-driver bundle. suspect IO scheduler interaction with new driver causing latency tail.

eve-support: ticket #C-4472 (AcmeCorp) — reported 22:07Z timeout on large embedding job (batch_size=512). They attached traces showing multiple retries. Customer is asking for ETA/mitigation.

ben.sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) route high-latency customer traffic off affected hosts (re-route to eu1-dedicated pool), 2) temporarily reduce max_batch_size for embeddings on eu1 to reduce nvme pressure, 3) enable prefix/KV cache warming for top customers to reduce disk reads, 4) rollback driver on a small set of hosts for canary.

alice.ops: agreed. plan: cordon eu1-03, eu1-12, eu1-19 (highest io) and drain; shift their traffic to eu1-dedicated via route policy override. reduce embeddings max_batch_size from 512 -> 128 for eu1. initiating now.

dmitri-eng: repro steps that triggered the contention locally: run fio with multiple jobs simulating our write pattern. example:

```
fio --name=burst --ioengine=libaio --iodepth=32 --rw=randwrite --bs=128k --size=10G --numjobs=8 --runtime=600 --direct=1 --filename=/dev/nvme0n1
```

this reproduces high queue depth and blk_mq complaints on the new driver. filing bug with vendor.

ben.sre: thanks — also ask release team if the cuda-driver bundle included any nvme firmware toggles. if so we need firmware rollback plan.

alice.ops: eve-support, please escalate AcmeCorp with mitigation note: we routed their jobs off the affected hosts and reduced batch_size; ask them to retry and provide logs. promise follow-up in 30m. :thumbsup:

eve-support: will do. adding note to ticket and sending exec summary.

dmitri-eng: starting rollback on eu1-03 as a canary (replacing driver package with previous build 524.9). will report back with iostat after rollback.

incidents-bot: runbook step executed: reroute-policy applied to `eu1/*` endpoints -> `eu1-dedicated-fallback`.

alice.ops: update 22:22Z — cordon/drain in progress for 3 hosts, routing policy applied, embeddings batch_size reduced. early telemetry shows p95 for embeddings in eu1 down to ~250-300ms (improved). p99 moving but still noisy. continuing rollback tests on canary. will update in 15m.

ben.sre: if rollback stabilizes canary, schedule rolling rollback in waves (3-5 hosts at a time) and keep routing fallback until fully mitigated. also prepare a postmortem checklist: kernel/driver matrix, nvme firmware versions, fio repro notes, and customer impact log.

alice.ops: noted. postmortem owners: ben.sre, dmitri-eng, carla-ml for validation. i'll start the incident doc.

eve-support: AcmeCorp updated — they saw retries succeed after reroute, asked for root cause once available.

dmitri-eng: canary rollback iostat after driver revert: nvme util -> 42%, avg await back to ~2-4ms. dmesg no longer showing blk_mq errors. looks promising.

alice.ops: good work team — keeping this thread as source of truth. next update at 22:40Z or sooner if things change. :heart:
